chapter: Style and solos in the early bands
title: Tyler's Beer Garden band with Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman
summary: The interviewer describes a 1945 band with saxophone, trumpet and tailgate trombone that never soloed.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You know, when I used to go out to Tyler's Beer Garden? Who? To Tyler's Beer Garden during the war. I don't think you were ever out there. No, I don't. But Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman had the band. Tillman played with us?
Tillman was playing saxophone. Tillman was playing saxophone.

Forty-five. Oh, no. I wasn't there. And Dude was playing trumpet with him, Foster and Brother. And Dude would take down, but the clarinet would, I mean the saxophone would carry the melody and the trombone would still play tailgate. And then Dude would come back. Who was on trombone?
But I never heard a solo the whole time I was there, you know.
I wondered how many bands there were like that that would, uh.
